persona.who: 39, Indian-American, two kids, runs a dental practice with her husband, loses her temper with the kids and hates herself after.
persona.note: I yelled at my 7 year old this morning for spilling milk and the look on his face. I am turning into my mother. I run a practice, I manage 12 people calmly, and then at home I just snap

understanding.emotion: ashamed and frightened of becoming her mother
understanding.bridge: The calm you show at work and the snap at home are not two different women. The texts call both the same mind, and they teach what to do with it.
understanding.week_thesis: The split between your work self and your home self is not your failure. The week shows you where the mind is held, and how to give it a different release.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the snap and the fear of becoming your mother, named without shame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the anger is not the verdict. The verdict is the mind that has no other release.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the self who snapped is the same self who can choose the next time.
week_beats.act: You try one pause before the next moment with him, and one breath that belongs only to you.
week_beats.story: A mother who snapped and then sat with the fear shows you how to meet the child after the storm.

understanding.core_struggle: A woman who leads calmly at work snaps at her child and is frightened she is becoming the mother she did not want to be.
understanding.mirror: You hold it together all day with twelve people, and the moment you are alone with your child, you lose it.
understanding.insight: It isn't that you are becoming your mother. It is that a mind that is held tight all day finds its only release at home, and then judges itself for the release.

verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna, on the battlefield, tells Krishna that the mind is restless, stormy, powerful and stubborn. He feels it is as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna does not tell him to simply calm down. He agrees the mind is difficult, but says practice and letting go can train it. The verse proposes that holding the mind is a skill learned through steady effort, not a single act of force.
verse.for_you: The snap at home and the calm at work come from the same mind. The fear of becoming your mother is the mind judging itself after it finds its only release. You do not need to become a different person.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
verse.line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
verse.translation: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that a person's mind is shaped by what it dwells upon. When you fix your attention on objects and outcomes, attachment forms. If that attachment is blocked, it hardens into anger. The verse traces this exact path from focus to frustration, showing that the mind is not the problem, but the direction of its gaze is. The steady person is the one who guards this attention, knowing that where the mind rests, the heart follows.
verse.for_you: You manage people calmly at work. That steadiness is real. The anger at home is not a verdict on your character. It is the result of a mind that has had no other release all day, and then turns on itself in the evening.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.

verse.line: Whoever can ride out the surge of desire and anger, here and now, is steady and happy.
verse.translation: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasang.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, describing the inner happiness of someone who sees clearly. He says that a person who can withstand the surge born of desire and anger, right here in this life, is truly disciplined and happy. This joy does not come from pleasures that start and end, but from finding a steady place within. The wise person sees that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and they are able to ride out these surges without being carried away.
verse.for_you: The same mind that snaps at your child is the one that can choose a different response. The texts say the self who gave in to anger is the same self who can decide to stand firm next time, right here in your own life.

verse.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verse.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verse.sanskrit: क्षेपाभिमानादभिषङ्गव्यलीकं निगृह्णाति ज्वलितं यश्च मन्युम् । अदुष्टचेता मुदितोऽनसूयुः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परेषाम् ॥
verse.line: Hold back the anger that flares at an insult; stay clean-hearted and cheerful.
verse.translation: One who holds back the blazing anger stirred by an insult or a wounding slight, who stays clean-hearted, cheerful and free of envy, takes the merit of others.
verse.why: When insulted, staying calm protects you more than hitting back.
verse.misuse: Holding back anger is not swallowing mistreatment; it is choosing how to respond.

prasang.title: How the swan answers insults
prasang.summary: The swan teaches that words are arrows, that answering insult with insult only inflames both sides, and that the person who stays calm and wishes no harm sleeps in peace while the insulter carries the damage.
prasang.lesson: When insulted, staying calm protects you more than hitting back.

verse.meaning: The golden swan taught the Sadhyas that when a wounding slight strikes, the blazing anger it stirs is a fire you can choose to hold back. To stay clean-hearted and cheerful in that moment is not weakness. It is a choice that protects your own peace and leaves you free of envy, while the one who threw the insult carries the damage.
verse.for_you: The snap at your child is the same mind that manages your practice calmly. It is not two women. The mind held tight all day seeks any release, and then judges itself for finding it at home.

verse.line: Don't answer anger with anger. The one who stays calm protects both people, and heals both.
verse.translation: One who does not get angry back at an angry person saves both himself and the other from great danger. He becomes the healer of both.

story.title: Kausalya and the child who ran from dinner
story.story_hook: Kausalya was shown the whole universe in her newborn, and all she wanted was for him to cry like a baby.
story.summary: At his birth Ram shows Kausalya his cosmic form, and she asks him instead to be simply a baby. Later scenes are pure childhood: the boy runs off mid-meal, curd on his face, dusty from play, while his father laughs and his mother chases him. When she once glimpses the whole universe in him again, she asks only to be spared that and keep her child.
story.lesson: The grandest thing about a child may be the ordinary hours of childhood itself.

script: You are carrying a quiet fear that you are becoming her. You are frightened by the snap, and ashamed of the gap between the calm you show at work and the sudden anger that reaches your child.
On the battlefield, Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless and powerful. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

The mind is not a wild horse to be tamed by force. It is a current that must be guided with steady practice. You cannot simply command it to stop. You train it by letting go, and by returning to the practice again and again. This is easier said than done, because the mind has been held tight all day at the practice. It does not release easily, and it judges itself for the release.
When you feel the tension rise after work, do not fight the anger. Step into the shower and let the water run until the heat leaves your shoulders. Let that be the letting go.
The calm at work and the snap at home are not two different women.

depth.life: You are home but not present. Your mind is still at work, holding everything together. Then a small thing breaks the surface and the anger comes out, and you are frightened it is the same anger you saw in your mother.
depth.points: The mind is not two different people. It is one mind held tight all day, and then it snaps. The anger is not a sign that you are becoming her. It is a sign that the mind has no other way to let go.
depth.practice: Sit for two minutes and let your hands rest. Do not try to calm the mind. Just notice where the tightness is in your body and let it be there.
depth.question: Where in your body do you feel the mind is still at work?
